title.en: Xia, Shang & Zhou: The Bronze Age
title.zh: 夏商周：早期国家与青铜文明

clips.send: About 1046 BCE King Wu of Zhou defeated King Zhou of Shang at the Battle of Muye. The Shang fell and the Western Zhou began, with its capital at Haojing (near Xi’an).
clips.text: About 1046 BCE King Wu of Zhou defeated King Zhou of Shang at the Battle of Muye. The Shang fell and the Western Zhou began, with its capital at Haojing (near Xi’an).

clips.send: Four rams. The rams’ bodies form the belly; their heads stick out. A ram stands at each of the four corners; its curled horns and head project from the shoulder. Late Shang dynasty; unearthed at Ningxiang, Hunan; 58.3 cm tall. Its unusual shape and exquisite craft make it a masterpiece of Shang bronze casting.

clips.send: Inscription “后母戊”. Three characters cast inside the wall. The inner wall carries three characters: 后母戊 (Hou Mu Wu). A Shang king had it cast to offer sacrifices to his mother, named “Wu”. Characters cast on bronzes are called bronze script (jinwen).

clips.send: The evolution of Chinese script: oracle-bone script, bronze script (cast on bronzes), small seal script (unified by the Qin), clerical script (Han), regular script.
clips.text: The evolution of Chinese script: oracle-bone script → bronze script (cast on bronzes) → small seal script (unified by the Qin) → clerical script (Han) → regular script.

clips.send: About 2070 BCE Yu founded the Xia, China’s first dynasty. After Yu died his son Qi took the throne: hereditary rule replaced abdication — “shared by all” became “owned by one family”.

clips.send: Upright handles (ears). Used to lift and carry the ding. Two upright “ears” stand on the rim of the short sides. Their outer sides are decorated with tigers and a human head. A pole could pass through them to carry the heavy vessel.

clips.send: Watch the pictures slowly turn into today’s square characters: sun 日, moon 月, mountain 山, person 人, tree 木. Chinese characters have developed continuously for over 3,000 years.

clips.send: Yin Ruins (Yinxu). Today: Anyang, Henan. Over 150,000 oracle bones with the earliest Chinese writing were dug up here, and the 832-kg Houmuwu Ding.
clips.text: Yin Ruins (Yinxu). Today: Anyang, Henan. Over 150,000 oracle bones with the earliest Chinese writing were dug up here, and the 832-kg Houmuwu Ding.

clips.send: Late Western Zhou rule decayed: in 841 BCE the people of the capital rose up. In 771 BCE the Western Zhou fell. The next year (770 BCE) King Ping moved the capital east to Luoyi — the Eastern Zhou began.

clips.send: Ding body and taotie pattern. A rectangular ritual cauldron of the late Shang. Cast in the late Shang dynasty; unearthed in 1939 at Anyang, Henan. It weighs 832.84 kg and stands 133 cm tall: the heaviest ancient Chinese bronze yet found. The walls are covered with beast-face (taotie) patterns on a background of thunder-cloud spirals.

clips.send: Four column legs. Hold up 832 kg — and leave room for a fire. Four thick hollow column legs support the vessel. A ding was first a cooking pot; later bronze ding became ritual vessels and symbols of power. Each leg is decorated with a beast face near the top.

clips.send: To secure its rule, the Zhou king gave land and people to royal relatives, meritorious officials and nobles of earlier dynasties, who set up vassal states such as Lu, Qi, Yan, Jin and Song. The lords had to obey, pay tribute, fight for the king and protect the royal house.

clips.send: Shang people carved writing on tortoise shells and animal bones to record divinations: oracle-bone script, the earliest known mature Chinese writing. Many characters are little pictures.

clips.send: National Museum of China. Today: East side of Tian’anmen Square, Beijing. One of the biggest museums in the world, with more than a million objects — from Neolithic pottery and the Houmuwu ding to treasures of every dynasty.

clips.send: A 1.6 m student (scale). Compare the sizes. The Houmuwu Ding (133 cm) is almost as tall as a middle-school student. The Four-Ram Zun (58.3 cm) reaches about up to the student’s thigh.

clips.send: Three dynasties in a row: Xia (about 2070–1600 BCE), Shang (about 1600–1046 BCE) and Western Zhou (about 1046–771 BCE).
clips.text: Three dynasties in a row: Xia (about 2070–1600 BCE), Shang (about 1600–1046 BCE) and Western Zhou (about 1046–771 BCE).

clips.send: Here on a schematic map: the Erlitou site near Yanshi, Henan may have been a Xia capital. About 1600 BCE Tang overthrew Xia and founded the Shang. About 1300 BCE King Pangeng moved the capital to Yin (Anyang) — after that Shang rule was stable.

clips.send: 后母戊鼎：鼎身与饕餮纹。 商朝晚期的长方形祭祀礼器。 商朝晚期铸造，1939 年在河南安阳出土。。 重 832.84 千克，高 133 厘米，是目前已发现的中国古代最重的青铜器。。 器身装饰着饕餮纹（兽面纹），底子是细密的云雷纹。

clips.send: 为了巩固统治，西周实行分封制：周王把土地和人民分封给王族、功臣和先代的贵族，让他们建立诸侯国，如鲁、齐、燕、晋、宋等。诸侯要服从周王命令，定期朝贡，带兵随从周王作战，保卫王室。
